name: Lokalise
tagline: Manage translation keys, screenshots, reviews, and CI sync for a small product team

tiers.name: Explorer
tiers.limits: Unlimited hosted words and translator/reviewer seats; plan-specific processed-word and advanced-seat allowances are not exposed as readable values on the live table
tiers.notes: Live page displays $144/mo; the yearly toggle is present but its alternate price did not render in accessible page text.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Unlimited hosted words and translator/reviewer seats; unlimited languages from Growth; processed-word overage purchasable
tiers.notes: Live page displays $375/mo; yearly price not verifiable from rendered text.

tiers.name: Advanced
tiers.limits: Unlimited hosted words and translator/reviewer seats; advanced seats scale by tier, with published range 5 to 100 across paid plans
tiers.notes: Live page displays $999/mo; yearly price not verifiable from rendered text.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom capacities, security, support and onboarding

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day Enterprise-feature trial, no credit card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; live page exposes the billing toggle but not the alternate yearly prices in readable text
pricing.hiddenCosts: Pricing scales on processed source words and advanced seats; processed-word overage and extra advanced seats are purchasable, while translator/reviewer seats and hosted words are unlimited.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Lokalise, manage translation keys, screenshots, reviews, and CI sync for a small product team. The hard boundary is integration breadth, translation memory, workflows, vendors, governance, and support, plus translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Manage translation keys, screenshots, and review work for a small product team, preserve context, import and export standard files, sync with CI, and publish approved strings.
requirements: optional DeepL or OpenAI API key
whatYouLose: integration breadth, translation memory, workflows, vendors, governance, and support
moatNotes: translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations
ongoingBurden: file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Lokalise because localization teams pay because language context, review discipline, translators, and release integrations are the hard parts. The recurring cost buys file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Tolgee
priorArt.desc: Active open-source localization platform with translation memory and in-context tooling.

alternatives.name: Tolgee
alternatives.desc: Keys, screenshots, review, translation memory and developer integrations without Lokalise's enterprise furniture.

facts.install: Hosted Tolgee Cloud signup or the official Docker Compose deployment with PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Tolgee's contextual AI translator and machine-translation layer can connect to Google Cloud Translation, Amazon Translate, DeepL, Microsoft Azure Translator, Baidu, and configured LLM/MT providers.
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted projects, keys, translations, users, and translation memory live in PostgreSQL, while screenshots and uploaded files live under the persistent data directory; cloud accounts store the same classes of data on Tolgee infrastructure.
facts.gapVsPaid: Tolgee covers a small product team's core but has a narrower enterprise integration catalog, branching workflow, mobile SDK/OTA delivery, vendor management, and support operation than Lokalise.
facts.setupBlocker: None for cloud signup; self-hosting needs Docker, an external PostgreSQL database, persistent file storage, mail/domain/TLS, backups, and provider keys for third-party translation engines.

alternatives.name: Weblate
alternatives.desc: Git-first string management with screenshots, memory, review and automation; less hand-holding, more control.

facts.install: Hosted Weblate signup or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.engines: Machine translation can connect to OpenAI/Azure OpenAI, DeepL, Google Cloud, Amazon Translate, Microsoft Translator, LibreTranslate, Baidu, Yandex, and other documented services.
facts.dataFormat: Translations, users, review state, memory, glossaries, and settings live in PostgreSQL; cloned source repositories and uploaded files live in persistent server volumes, with Valkey/Redis used for queues and caches.
facts.gapVsPaid: Weblate is more repository-centric and operator-heavy, with less polished screenshot workflow, design-tool integration, OTA/mobile delivery, and onboarding than Lokalise.
facts.setupBlocker: Cloud hosting is free only for qualifying libre projects; the general free route requires Docker, PostgreSQL, Valkey/Redis, domain/TLS, mail, repository credentials, backups, and upgrades.

alternatives.name: Mozilla Pontoon
alternatives.desc: Repository-backed translation, suggestions and review from Mozilla's own battle-tested localization machinery.

facts.install: Docker setup is documented for development; production deployment must be adapted from Mozilla/Heroku-style infrastructure
facts.dataFormat: Projects sync translations to version-control repositories, while users, suggestions, reviews, translation memory, and job state live in Pontoon's server databases and caches; Mozilla's public instance is not a general hosted service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Pontoon lacks Lokalise's turnkey hosted onboarding, broad CI/design/mobile integrations, branch management, commercial support, and supported general-purpose deployment.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is that the official Docker stack is explicitly not for production and the project does not provide a turnkey supported deployment for arbitrary operators.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Essential plan and a small-team string-management system DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Lokalise in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one optional machine-translation API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage translation keys, screenshots, and review work for a small product team, preserve context, import and export standard files, sync with CI, and publish approved strings.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement projects, locales, keys, namespaces, descriptions, screenshots, translations, and review status.
Import and export JSON, YAML, PO, and XLIFF while preserving placeholders and plural forms.
Add glossary checks, missing-string filters, translation memory, comments, and reviewer assignment.
Use machine translation only on selected strings and show provider, cost, and source text before approval.
Provide token-authenticated pull and push endpoints for CI with an immutable change log.
Add backups, locale deletion safeguards, and a pseudo-localization preview.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a translator labor marketplace.
Deliberately leave out a global website translation proxy.
Deliberately leave out enterprise integrations, legal translation assurance, and round-the-clock support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
